newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals tumble, palladium mostly up.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals tumble, palladium mostly up.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures, except for the palladium contract, dived on Tuesday, due to active long-liquidation after the yen rose strongly against the dollar, traders said.
Five contract months of gold futures, including the benchmark April, fell by their 40 yen per gram daily limit at the close. Benchmark April gold was off 40 yen at 1,235 yen.
October, February and April platinum tumbled by their 50 yen daily limit. Benchmark platinum closed at 1,348 yen.
"The focus is on the FOMC meeting later on Tuesday, which should determine the currency direction," one trader said.
Spot gold was quoted at $341.95/342.45 per ounce at 0724 GMT, against $341.30/90 in New York on Monday.
The dollar dipped below 113 yen in late Tokyo trade after falling nearly three yen from its New York close.

"Views that the dollar has more room to dip may prompt local investors to sell gold and platinum futures," one trader said. Monday's report by Johnson Matthey forecasting strong growth in palladium demand in auto catalysts and sharply rising offtake for platinum jewellery in China was a positive factor for platinum group metals, but the impact faded later as the yen climbed strongly, the traders said.
